description: European cultural and intellectual rebirth from the 14th to 17th centuries

overview.meaning: French for 'rebirth'; revival of classical Greek and Roman culture

italian_renaissance.florence: Center of Renaissance; Medici family as patrons of arts
italian_renaissance.venice: Maritime trade city; Venetian school of painting
italian_renaissance.medici_family: Banking dynasty that sponsored artists including Botticelli, Michelangelo, Leonardo da Vinci

michelangelo.techniques: Contrapposto stance, emotional intensity, monumental scale

techniques.perspective: Linear perspective creates illusion of depth (Brunelleschi, Alberti)
techniques.sfumato: Leonardo's blending technique for soft edges
techniques.chiaroscuro: Use of light and dark contrast for depth

literature_and_philosophy.erasmus: Northern Renaissance humanist; In Praise of Folly

scientific_revolution_links.copernicus: Heliocentric model (1543); Earth orbits the Sun
scientific_revolution_links.galileo: Telescope, laws of motion, supported heliocentrism
scientific_revolution_links.vesalius: Modern anatomy; De Humani Corporis Fabrica (1543)
scientific_revolution_links.printing_press: Gutenberg's movable type (~1450) spread Renaissance ideas across Europe

literature.shakespeare: England; greatest playwright; Hamlet, Macbeth, Romeo and Juliet
literature.cervantes: Spain; Don Quixote; first modern novel
